9701_m18_qp_12:q30.solve: The absorption near 1200 cm⁻¹ indicates C–O stretching, while that near 3400 cm⁻¹ indicates O–H stretching. Both are required, so count alcohols, not ethers. A.pathway: Identified the required functional group as an alcohol but counted only butan-1-ol and butan-2-ol, overlooking alcohols with a branched carbon skeleton.

followup.stem: Compare CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂OH and (CH₃)₂CHCH₂OH. Which statement is correct?

options.A: They are the same compound drawn in different orientations.
options.B: They have different molecular formulae because one carbon skeleton is branched.
options.C: They are structural isomers with molecular formula C₄H₁₀O, and both are alcohols.
options.D: The first compound is an alcohol, but the second is an ether.

followup.why: Branching changes the carbon connectivity without changing the molecular formula or removing the C–O and O–H bonds, so branched alcohols must also be considered.

C.pathway: Counted placing –OH at positions 1, 2, 3 and 4 along the unbranched four-carbon chain as four different structures, then added the two branched alcohols to obtain six.

followup.stem: When counting structural isomers, how should CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃ and CH₃CH₂CH(OH)CH₃ be treated?

options.A: They are two positional isomers because –OH appears at different positions when read from the left.
options.B: They represent one structural isomer because reversing the chain preserves the connectivity.
options.C: They are two chain isomers because their carbon skeletons differ.
options.D: They are functional group isomers because one is an alcohol and the other is an ether.

followup.why: Both drawings represent butan-2-ol, since numbering from the nearer end gives the –OH group position 2 in either drawing.

D.pathway: Used only the C–O absorption requirement and counted all seven C₄H₁₀O structural isomers, including the three ethers, without checking for the O–H absorption.

followup.stem: Ethanol, CH₃CH₂OH, and methoxymethane, CH₃OCH₃, both contain C–O bonds. Which statement about an O–H stretching absorption near 3400 cm⁻¹ is correct for pure samples?

options.A: Only ethanol can give this absorption because it contains an O–H bond.
options.B: Only methoxymethane can give this absorption because its oxygen is bonded to two carbon atoms.
options.C: Both can give this absorption because both contain oxygen.
options.D: Neither can give this absorption because neither contains a C=O bond.

followup.why: A C–O bond does not guarantee an O–H bond: ethanol has both, whereas methoxymethane has no O–H bond.

followup.stem: Which assignment is characteristic of a strong IR absorption at 1710 cm⁻¹?

options.B: It is due to C–H stretching.
options.C: It is due to C–O single-bond stretching.
options.D: It is due to C=O stretching.

followup.stem: Which statement correctly assigns a broad IR absorption around 3000 cm⁻¹?

options.B: An absorption at 2200–2250 cm−1 is characteristic of C≡N stretching.
options.C: A broad absorption at 3200–3600 cm−1 is characteristic of C≡N stretching.
options.D: An absorption at 1640–1750 cm−1 identifies C≡N stretching.

followup.why: C≡N stretching is identified by its characteristic wavenumber range, 2200–2250 cm−1, not merely by a trough being sharp.

B.pathway: Treated low transmittance as weak absorption, so dismissed the deep trough in the carbonyl region and concluded that neither group was detected.

followup.stem: An infrared spectrum has percentage transmittance on its vertical axis. What does a deep downward trough indicate?

options.A: The sample strongly absorbs infrared radiation at that wavenumber.
options.B: The sample transmits almost all the incident infrared radiation at that wavenumber.
options.C: The sample has no vibration capable of absorbing infrared radiation at that wavenumber.
options.D: The sample emits infrared radiation at that wavenumber rather than absorbing it.

followup.why: Low transmittance means little incident radiation passes through the sample, so a deep downward trough represents strong absorption.

D.pathway: Assigned the strong absorption in the carbonyl region to C≡N instead of C=O, substituting the nitrile bond label for the carbonyl bond label.

followup.stem: Which bond assignment matches the characteristic infrared stretching range 1640–1750 cm−1?

options.A: This range is characteristic of C≡N stretching.
options.B: This range is characteristic of C–H stretching.
options.C: This range is characteristic of O–H stretching.
options.D: This range is characteristic of C=O stretching.

9701_s19_qp_13:q2.solve: The peaks at m/e 63 and 65 represent copper isotopes, while the peak at 197 represents gold. To find Aᵣ of copper, calculate the abundance-weighted mean using only the copper isotopes. Their abundances are percentages of the whole alloy, so divide by their combined abundance, 56.36 + 25.14, rather than by 100. Thus Aᵣ(Cu) = [(56.36 × 63) + (25.14 × 65)] / (56.36 + 25.14), giving option C and approximately 63.62.

A.pathway: The student excludes gold from the weighted mass total but fails to exclude its abundance from the denominator, treating whole-alloy percentages as percentages within copper.

followup.stem: The copper-63 and copper-65 peaks have abundances 56.36 and 25.14 on the whole-alloy scale. Which statement gives the fraction of copper atoms that are copper-63?
followup.why: A fraction within copper must use the total abundance of copper atoms, 56.36 + 25.14, as its denominator.

B.pathway: The student applies the weighted-mean rule to every atom represented in the alloy spectrum, calculating a mean for the mixture instead of for copper alone.

followup.stem: More gold is added to this alloy without changing the copper isotope ratio. Which statement about Aᵣ of the copper is correct?

options.A: It stays unchanged because the copper isotope masses and their ratio are unchanged.
options.B: It increases because gold atoms are heavier than copper atoms.
options.C: It decreases because copper makes up a smaller fraction of the alloy.
options.D: It becomes the mean relative mass of all copper and gold atoms in the alloy.

followup.why: Aᵣ of copper depends only on the masses and relative proportions of copper isotopes, not on how much gold accompanies them.

followup.stem: For an isotope-weighted mean, the numerator is the sum of each isotope's relative mass multiplied by its abundance. Which division completes the calculation?

options.A: Divide by the sum of the relative isotope masses.
options.B: Divide by the number of isotopes included.
options.C: Divide by the abundance of the most abundant isotope.
options.D: Divide by the sum of the abundances of the isotopes included.

followup.why: A weighted mean divides the weighted total by the sum of its weights, which here are the isotope abundances.

9701_s22_qp_11:q40.solve: Match the information required to what each technique measures. Infrared spectroscopy detects absorption associated with bond vibrations, so characteristic absorptions can identify functional groups in organic compounds. Mass spectrometry measures ions by their mass-to-charge ratios and provides information about molecular mass, isotopes and fragmentation. Although a mass spectrometer produces ions, it does not measure successive ionisation energies; infrared spectroscopy does not measure these either. Therefore, A is the best choice.

B.pathway: The student treats mass-spectral fragment information as equivalent to the characteristic bond absorptions used to identify functional groups by infrared spectroscopy.

followup.stem: Which statement correctly describes a characteristic absorption band in an organic compound's infrared spectrum?

options.A: It arises when bonds absorb radiation and change their vibrational energy.
options.B: It directly measures the mass-to-charge ratio of a fragment ion.
options.C: It directly measures the relative abundance of an isotope.
options.D: It arises when the instrument separates molecular ions according to mass-to-charge ratio.

followup.why: Infrared bands arise from molecular vibrations, whereas ion mass-to-charge ratios and isotope abundances are mass-spectrometric information.

C.pathway: The student recognises that infrared absorption involves energy and extends this to measuring successive ionisation energies, overlooking the difference between bond vibration and electron removal.

followup.stem: Which statement defines the first ionisation energy of sodium?

options.A: It is the energy required to remove one electron from each atom in one mole of gaseous Na atoms.
options.B: It is the energy required to excite bond vibrations in one mole of sodium-containing molecules.
options.C: It is the energy required to remove one proton from each atom in one mole of gaseous Na atoms.
options.D: It is the energy required to remove one electron from each ion in one mole of gaseous Na+ ions.

followup.why: First ionisation removes electrons from gaseous atoms, not by exciting bond vibrations; removing electrons from Na+ instead defines the second ionisation energy.

D.pathway: The student uses the fact that mass spectrometry involves ionisation to conclude that it measures the energies required for successive electron removals.

followup.stem: Which statement correctly describes what a conventional mass spectrometer measures?

options.A: It measures the mass-to-charge ratios and relative abundances of detected ions.
options.B: It directly measures the energy needed to remove each successive electron from an atom.
options.C: It measures the characteristic infrared absorption frequencies of bonds.
options.D: It directly measures the energy needed to break each bond in a molecule.

followup.why: Producing ions is a step in mass spectrometry, but the measured ion information is mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance, not successive ionisation energies.

9701_s22_qp_12:q40.solve: For a singly charged fragment ion, m/e equals its relative mass; different fragment formulas can therefore give the same m/e. Ethanal can lose a neutral H atom to form CH3CO+, with mass 24 + 3 + 16 = 43. Either propanol can undergo C–O bond cleavage, losing a neutral OH radical and forming C3H7+, with mass 36 + 7 = 43. The question requires a fragment peak, not necessarily the largest peak. All three compounds qualify, so the answer is D.

A.pathway: Recognised CH3CO+ from ethanal but treated m/e = 43 as exclusive to that oxygen-containing fragment, overlooking C3H7+ from the alcohols.

followup.stem: Using Ar values C = 12, H = 1 and O = 16, which statement about these singly charged fragment ions is correct?

options.A: CH3CO+ has m/e = 43, but C3H7+ does not.
options.B: C3H7+ has m/e = 43, but CH3CO+ does not.
options.C: Both CH3CO+ and C3H7+ have m/e = 43.
options.D: Neither CH3CO+ nor C3H7+ has m/e = 43.

followup.why: CH3CO+ has mass 24 + 3 + 16 = 43 and C3H7+ has mass 36 + 7 = 43, so this m/e does not uniquely identify one fragment formula.

B.pathway: Accepted the fragments from ethanal and propan-1-ol, but miscounted [(CH3)2CH]+ from propan-2-ol as C3H6+, overlooking the central carbon's H atom and assigning m/e = 42.

followup.stem: A singly charged fragment has the structure [(CH3)2CH]+. Using Ar values C = 12 and H = 1, which statement is correct?

options.A: It contains six H atoms and has m/e = 42.
options.B: It contains seven H atoms and has m/e = 43.
options.C: It contains eight H atoms and has m/e = 44.
options.D: It contains five H atoms and has m/e = 41.

followup.why: The two CH3 groups contribute six H atoms and the central CH contributes one, giving C3H7+ with m/e = 36 + 7 = 43.

C.pathway: Accepted OH-radical loss from both alcohols but restricted fragmentation to loss of groups containing heavier atoms, rejecting loss of a single H atom from ethanal.

followup.stem: Which statement about fragmentation of an ethanal molecular ion is correct?

options.A: Loss of a neutral H atom can give CH3CO+ at m/e = 43.
options.B: A fragment ion cannot form unless the carbon–carbon bond breaks.
options.C: Loss of a neutral H atom must leave an uncharged fragment.
options.D: Loss of a neutral H atom leaves the ion's mass unchanged.

followup.why: Losing a neutral H atom preserves the positive charge while reducing the ethanal ion's mass from 44 to 43, forming CH3CO+.

followup.stem: Bromine has isotopes ⁷⁹Br and ⁸¹Br. Which statement about the intact, singly charged mixed-isotope ion ⁷⁹Br⁸¹Br⁺ is correct?

followup.stem: Bromine has isotopes ⁷⁹Br and ⁸¹Br. Ignoring fragments, which statement correctly counts the peaks from intact, singly charged Br₂⁺ ions?

options.A: There are three peaks, corresponding to total masses 158, 160 and 162.
